pyramid.label: Purpose
pyramid.statement: Founders build better companies when they learn from founders who have been there.
proof: Brad Feld's Boulder Thesis, from his book Startup Communities, holds that entrepreneurs must lead a startup community.
A Kauffman Foundation study, summarized in the same post, found high demand among entrepreneurs for peer-based learning and networking.

pyramid.label: Vision
pyramid.statement: Every Colorado founder knows where to turn.
proof: The welcome desk offers eight doors, from an idea to just curious, and points each visitor to a first step.
Startup Resources maps Colorado help by company stage, from a first idea to a growing company.

pyramid.label: Mission
pyramid.statement: Unite and help founders as they build the next generation of Colorado companies.
proof: The founder's bio on the Team page names the same focus: uniting and helping founders as they build the next generation of Colorado companies.
The Oct 6, 2026 dispatch names uniting and helping founders as the focus now.

pyramid.label: Values
pyramid.statement: Founders first, A door for everyone, Ask and offer, Show the source, People lead

items.name: Founders first
items.means: Every page, line and channel speaks to founders before anyone else.
items.proof: The welcome desk opens with the three founder doors (idea, building, hiring), and the founders forum is for founders only.

items.name: A door for everyone
items.means: The people who back founders, and anyone curious, are welcome and shown where they fit.
items.proof: The welcome desk has eight doors, from founders to students and the just curious, and the Slack is free to join.

items.name: Ask and offer
items.means: Bring what you need, give what you can, and do both in the open.
items.proof: Every Wednesday, asks and offers go in one thread in the Slack and the LinkedIn Group, where founders answer founders.

items.name: Show the source
items.means: Every claim can be checked: a link for each listing, a source for each figure.
items.proof: Every Leaderboard listing links to the sources used, and Resourcus cites only resources on the map and says so when nothing fits.

items.name: People lead
items.means: People run the community. The AI keepers help, say they are AI, and never moderate.
items.proof: Every moderator and organizer seat is for a person, and the site's footer names each keeper as an AI agent.

pyramid.label: Positioning
pyramid.statement: For founders building in Colorado, Colorado Startups is the open community, free to join and there every day, where founders meet founders and find what their company needs next.

pyramid.label: Promise
pyramid.statement: Come in, meet the founders already building here and find what your company needs next.

organizations.name: Colorado Startups
organizations.why: Founders first; the people who back them are welcome second. The Slack is free to join through an invite form; a person approves each LinkedIn Group member.

organizations.name: Colorado Startup Week
organizations.why: Speaks to entrepreneurs, investors, creatives and changemakers alike. Free and open to all.

organizations.name: Boulder Startup Week
organizations.why: Bills itself as a conference for entrepreneurs. Free.

organizations.name: 1 Million Cups Denver
organizations.why: A Kauffman Foundation program for local entrepreneurs, with a Denver chapter. A public morning meetup on the community calendar; no fee is listed.

organizations.name: Startup Colorado
organizations.why: Serves rural founders and the ecosystem builders who support them. An online community anyone can join; program fees are not stated on its pages.

organizations.name: Colorado Startup Resources
organizations.why: Built for Colorado founders, with listings organizations can claim. Free basic accounts; a paid partner plan for listed organizations.

organizations.name: Exponential Impact
organizations.why: Calls itself founder-first, for emerging-tech founders. The weekly Tech Connect coffee is open; the accelerator takes founders by application.

organizations.name: Techstars Boulder Accelerator
organizations.why: Backs founders and their companies. Founders apply by a deadline and are selected into a cohort.

organizations.name: Innosphere
organizations.why: Serves science and technology startups, plus regional ecosystem programs. Companies apply to its accelerator.

organizations.name: Venture Partners at CU Boulder
organizations.why: Serves university researchers, inventors and creators. Several workshops are open to anyone; others are for teams commercializing CU work.

organizations.name: New Tech Colorado
organizations.why: For technologists, founders, investors and students who want to see what is next in tech. A public Meetup group with RSVPs; no fee is listed.

organizations.name: Colorado SBDC Network
organizations.why: Serves small businesses of every type; startups are one group among many. No-cost, confidential advising for any eligible small business.

organizations.name: Built In Colorado
organizations.why: Serves tech professionals and the employers hiring them. Free to browse; employers reach candidates through a paid hiring membership (inferred from its Hire Now link).

organizations.name: Colorado Technology Association
organizations.why: Speaks for the tech industry, from startups to major employers, including on policy. Paid membership tiers.

organizations.name: Rockies Venture Club
organizations.why: Built around angel investors; startups apply to pitch them. Membership tiers for investors, startups and companies; startups apply to pitch.

organizations.name: Elevate Quantum
organizations.why: Serves the quantum industry: shared lab space, facilities and workforce training. Companies lease lab space and join its workforce consortium.

traits.name: Warm
traits.means: Kind and glad you came. We thank people by name and never gush.

traits.name: Direct
traits.means: Answer first. Short sentences, one idea each, and words that do what they say.

traits.name: Specific
traits.means: One specific thing beats a general claim. A named founder, company, city or sourced number, stated accurately.

traits.name: Bright
traits.means: Hopeful and lit by gold, fire and light. The lore is used lightly, and clarity always wins.

channels.label: Website
channels.note: Lore words in headings and keeper lines. Forms, policies and errors stay literal.

channels.label: Slack
channels.note: Short, friendly and useful. Founders first; service providers bring offers to the Wednesday thread.

channels.label: Startupers newsletter
channels.note: Colorado wins, a builder lesson and upcoming events, each win with a name, a city and a source.

channels.label: LinkedIn
channels.note: Sponsors and press read LinkedIn, so the words stay Core; world art may appear in images. No engagement bait.

channels.label: Sponsor email
channels.note: One ask, stated in the first line. Every figure sourced.

channels.label: State or partner documents
channels.note: No lore and no keeper lines. Never imply that a government or partner backs Colorado Startups. Co-branded layouts follow data/architecture.yaml.

channels.label: Error messages
channels.note: Say what went wrong and how to fix it. No apology, no blame, no lore.

channels.label: Keeper lines
channels.note: First person, plain modern English, with the keeper's disclosure beside it.

boilerplates.text: Colorado Startups is a community of founders building companies in Colorado. Founders come first; the people who join, back and serve them are welcome too.

Colorado Startups is a community of founders building companies in Colorado. Founders come first; the people who join, back and serve them are welcome too. Paul Foley founded it in 2014. The community meets in its Slack and LinkedIn Group, and its website charts Colorado startup resources for every stage.

Colorado Startups is a community of founders building companies in Colorado. Founders come first; the people who join, back and serve them are welcome too. Paul Foley founded it in 2014, and Colorado Startups, Ltd. runs it from Denver. The community calls itself Startupers and meets in its Slack and LinkedIn Group. Its website charts startup resources for every stage. Three regions, Photon Mountain, Space Peak and Fusion Canyon, connect founders from Fort Collins to Colorado Springs. AI agents help on the website, and each says it is an AI agent. Only people moderate the groups or hold its seats.

style: No em dashes and no spaced en dashes. Use a comma, semicolon, period or parentheses. An unspaced en dash in a range is fine.
One idea per sentence. Split any sentence past 30 words.
Every figure carries its source in the same sentence, or the word "goal".
At most one exclamation mark on a page.
UI copy is in sentence case. Buttons say exactly what happens, such as "Join the Slack" or "Nominate a company".
Write "Startupers" as one word with a capital S.
Write "Colorado Startups" in public copy. "CS" is for internal notes only.
Never call any place "the Silicon Valley of" anything. Say what its founders build.
A sentence that names a keeper also says "AI agent". The full rule is keepers.disclosure_rule in data/voice.yaml.
Lore words stay out of forms, buttons, policies and errors. The vocabulary rule in data/voice.yaml says where they go.

glossary.means: The community of founders building companies in Colorado, and Colorado Startups, Ltd., which runs it. Paul Foley founded it in 2014.
The plain look and voice (logo, palette, type, plain layout) for sponsors, government and partner documents, press and decks.
The look and voice with materials, keepers, art and lore, for the website, Slack, the newsletter and events.
The sentence each keeper carries wherever it appears, copied word for word from dwarves.yaml.
The website's word for the three areas: Photon Mountain (Boulder, Golden, Arvada, Denver), Space Peak (Colorado Springs, Fountain) and Fusion Canyon (Fort Collins, Loveland, Windsor).
A role a person fills, such as moderator, organizer, Slack Community Lead or Connector. Keepers never hold one.
An unpaid volunteer seat that connects the founders in one region.
The website's directory of Colorado programs, investors and services, sorted by company stage. It was called the Ecosystem Canvas.
Colorado companies the community recognizes, ranked from verified data. It ranks companies, never people.
The website's news log, newest first.
The website's first stop. A visitor picks a door, and Communitas, an AI agent, points them to the right place to start.
One of the eight choices on the welcome desk: idea, building, hiring, talent, investing, service provider, student and curious.
A fixed arrangement of the logo and a name, such as "Colorado Startups · Golden".
The line "a Colorado Startups project", set with Photon Mountain, Space Peak and Fusion Canyon, which keep their own looks.
The everyday word set beside a lore word, such as "keeper (AI helper)".
Approved about-text at a fixed length, ready to paste.
How loud one voice trait is on one channel, from 0 to 100.
The check that blocks every term in the never list of data/words.yaml.
The website's checklist for newcomers. Finishing it earns an honor card.
A card that names what someone did. The person can hide it, and it shows no counts.
The website's page at /agents/, labelled "AI agents", for the community's open-source AI agent projects.
A figure for one region, such as members or gatherings. Tallies sit side by side and are never ranked; regions are equals.
Places that matter to the Ute and other tribes, such as Garden of the Gods, are never fantasy decoration.
